AE.Unnamed: 2: Were any adverse events experienced? [en]
AE.Unnamed: 11:
AEYN [CDASH]
Indicate if the subject experienced any adverse events. If yes, include the appropriate details where indicated on the CRF. [completionInstructions]
The intent/purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring. It provides verification that all other fields on the CRF were deliberately left blank. [implementationNotes]
Does not map to an SDTMIG variable. The SDTM aCRF is annotated to indicate that this field is NOT SUBMITTED. [mappingInstructions]
Any Adverse Events [prompt]

AE.Unnamed: 2: What is the adverse event term? [en]
AE.Unnamed: 11:
AETERM [CDASH]
Record only 1 diagnosis, sign or symptom per line (e.g., nausea and vomiting should not be recorded in the same entry, but as 2 separate entries). Using accepted medical terminology, enter the diagnosis (if known); otherwise enter a sign or symptom. [completionInstructions]
Can be represented either as an open-entry field to capture verbatim terms reported by subjects or could be preprinted in the situation where solicited AEs of interest are captured. In most cases, the verbatim term (i.e., investigator-reported term) will be coded to a standard medical dictionary such as MedDRA or WHO ART, after the data have been collected on the CRF. [implementationNotes]
Maps directly to the SDTMIG variable listed in the column with the heading SDTMIG Target. [mappingInstructions]
Adverse Event [prompt]

AE.Unnamed: 2:
What is the adverse event start date?
Start Date [en]
AE.Unnamed: 11:
AESTDAT [CDASH]
Record the start date of the AE using this format (DD-MON-YYYY). [completionInstructions]
This does not map directly to an SDTMIG variable. For the SDTM submission dataset, concatenate all collected CDASH START DATE and TIME components and populate the SDTMIG variable AESTDTC in ISO 8601 format. [mappingInstructions]
Start Date [prompt]

AE.Unnamed: 2:
Is the adverse event ongoing (as of [the study-specific time point     or period])?
Ongoing [en]
AE.Unnamed: 11:
AEONGO [CDASH]
Indicate if the adverse event has not resolved at the time of data collection; leave the End Date blank. [completionInstructions]
Completed to indicate that the AE has not resolved at the time of data collection, when no End Date is collected. In some cases the ongoing status may be determined from AE Outcome. The purpose of collecting this field is to help with data cleaning and monitoring; this field provides further confirmation that the End Date was deliberately left blank. Often used as a tick/checkbox. [implementationNotes]
This does not map directly to an SDTMIG variable. May be used to populate a value into an SDTMIG relative timing variable such as AEENRF or AEENRTPT. When populating AEENRF, if the value of AEONGO is "Y", the value of "DURING", "AFTER" or "DURING/AFTER" may be used. When populating AEENRTPT, if the value of AEONGO is "Y", the value of "ONGOING" may be used. When AEONGO refers to the Study Reference Period (defined in DM.RFSTDTC to DM.RFENDTC) the SDTMIG variable AEENRF should be populated. When AEONGO is compared to another time point, the SDTMIG variables AEENRTPT and AEENTPT should be used. Note: AEENRTPT must refer to a time point anchor described in AEENTPT. [mappingInstructions]
Ongoing (as of [the study-specific time point or period]) [prompt]

AE.Unnamed: 2:
What was the adverse event end date?
End Date [en]
AE.Unnamed: 11:
AEENDAT [CDASH]
Record the date that the AE resolved using this format (DD-MON-YYYY). If the AE is ongoing, leave the field blank. [completionInstructions]
The definition of resolved is sponsor-specific. The preferred method is to collect a complete end date (if applicable). Partial dates (e.g., providing year only, month and year only) may be acceptable. [implementationNotes]
This does not map directly to an SDTMIG variable. For the SDTM submission dataset, concatenate all collected CDASH END DATE and TIME components and populate the SDTMIG variable AEENDTC in ISO 8601 format. [mappingInstructions]
End Date [prompt]

AE.Unnamed: 2:
What is the severity of the adverse event?
Severity [en]
AE.Unnamed: 11:
AESEV [CDASH]
The reporting physician/healthcare professional will assess the severity of the event using the sponsor-defined categories. This assessment is subjective and the reporting physician/ healthcare professional should use medical judgment to compare the reported AE to similar type events observed in clinical practice. Severity is not equivalent to seriousness. [completionInstructions]
Either AESEV or AETOXGR must appear on the CRF. Some studies may mandate the collection of both. Refer to ICH E3 Section 12.2.4 guidelines for Clinical Study Reports. [implementationNotes]
Maps directly to the SDTMIG variable listed in the column with the heading SDTMIG Target. [mappingInstructions]
Severity [prompt]

AE.Unnamed: 2: Was the adverse event serious? [en]
AE.Unnamed: 11:
AESER [CDASH]
Assess if an adverse event should be classified as serious based on the serious criteria defined in the protocol. [completionInstructions]
This field is related to the individual serious adverse event type fields, which may or may not be collected on the CRF. Either AESER or all the Adverse Serious type fields must be present on the CRF. The sponsor should check if the regulatory agencies to which the data will be submitted require the collection of this data. [implementationNotes]
Maps directly to the SDTMIG variable listed in the column with the heading SDTMIG Target. [mappingInstructions]
Serious [prompt]

AE.Unnamed: 2: Did the adverse event result in death? [en]
AE.Unnamed: 11:
AESDTH [CDASH]
Record whether the serious adverse event resulted in death. [completionInstructions]
If the details regarding Serious AEs are collected in the clinical database, then it is recommended that a separate Yes/No variable be defined for each Serious AE type. Sponsors may only collect the AESER field because the individual serious adverse event types might be collected in a separate pharmacovigilance database and therefore are not collected in the clinical database. The sponsor should check if the regulatory agencies to which the data will be submitted require the collection of this data. [implementationNotes]
Maps directly to the SDTMIG variable listed in the column with the heading SDTMIG Target. [mappingInstructions]
Death [prompt]

AE.Unnamed: 2:
Was this adverse event related to study treatment?
Relationship to Study Treatment [en]
AE.Unnamed: 11:
AEREL [CDASH]
Indicate if the cause of the adverse event is related to the study treatment and cannot be reasonably explained by other factors (e.g., subject's clinical state, concomitant therapy, other interventions). [completionInstructions]
Sponsored-defined controlled terminology is used to indicate the relationship between the AE and the study treatment (e.g., ICH E2B examples include "Not Related", "Unlikely Related", "Possibly Related", "Related"). Another possibility is the use of "Y" and "N". CDISC Controlled Terminology may be defined in the future. It is recommended that sponsors check with the appropriate regulatory authority for population of this variable to ensure it meets expectations for submission. [implementationNotes]
Maps directly to the SDTMIG variable listed in the column with the heading SDTMIG Target. [mappingInstructions]
Relationship to Study Treatment [prompt]

AE.Unnamed: 2:
What action was taken with study treatment?
Action Taken with Study Treatment [en]
AE.Unnamed: 11:
AEACN [CDASH]
Record changes made to the study treatment resulting from the adverse event. [completionInstructions]
CDISC Controlled Terminology is used to indicate the action taken with the study treatment in response to the AE. How to handle multiple actions taken is a sponsor-specific decision. If this information is collected elsewhere (e.g., on the Exposure CRF), then it is not required to be collected on the AE CRF. This variable is not to be used for actions taken with devices. See the SDTMIG for Medical Devices for information on reporting multiple actions, or actions with multiple devices. [implementationNotes]
Maps directly to the SDTMIG variable listed in the column with the heading SDTMIG Target. [mappingInstructions]
Action Taken with Study Treatment [prompt]

AE.Unnamed: 2:
What other action was taken?
Other Action Taken [en]
AE.Unnamed: 11:
AEACNOTH [CDASH]
Record all other action(s) taken resulting from the adverse event that are unrelated to study treatments given because of this adverse event. [completionInstructions]
This field is usually collected as a free text field. If possible/desired, the sponsor can create controlled terminology (e.g., Treatment Unblinded, Primary Care Physician Notified). [implementationNotes]
Maps directly to the SDTMIG variable listed in the column with the heading SDTMIG Target. [mappingInstructions]
Other Action Taken [prompt]

AE.Unnamed: 2:
What is the outcome of this adverse event?
Outcome [en]
AE.Unnamed: 11:
AEOUT [CDASH]
Record the appropriate outcome of the event in relation to the subject's status. [completionInstructions]
CDISC Controlled Terminology is used to indicate the outcome of the event as it relates to the subject's status. The Outcome controlled terminology includes ICH E2B values. The use of this field is the recommended way to describe whether and how the AE resolved. Since the outcome of an AE may be "Death", if this field is NOT used, be sure to provide another form, such as Disposition, with clear instructions to record deaths there. [implementationNotes]
Maps directly to the SDTMIG variable listed in the column with the heading SDTMIG Target. [mappingInstructions]
